events.title: SCT Presents ‘Leonardo! A Wonderful Show About a Terrible Monster’
events.loc: Seattle Children’s Theatre , 201 Thomas St., Seattle
events.desc: I took my daughter to see this production last weekend, and she’s already asking when we can go back. This is such a unique and joyful show based on two of our favorite books by Mo Willems. The pages truly come to life with talented actors and puppeteers. My tip: Come early for activities in the lobby, including shadow puppets and monster drawing, and plan for extra time to browse the adorable …

events.title: Tacoma Greek Festival
events.loc: St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church , 1523 Yakima Ave., Tacoma
events.desc: My usual takeout order lately has been gyros and Greek fries. You can try both (along with calamari, spanakopita and more!) at this lively festival. While you’re there, tour the beautiful church and enjoy folkloric dance performances.

events.title: A Very Farmy Halloween Edition
events.cost: $35 per person; children 2 and younger free
events.loc: Luckie Farms , 930 Sunnyside Blvd., Lake Stevens
events.desc: I cannot imagine a more perfect fall day than one spent cuddling Scottish Highland cows. This sweet farm invites guests to pet and feed the cows, reindeer, yaks, alpacas, horses and mini donkeys. (Swoon!) Tour the farm, take selfies with the animals and enjoy the slower pace. Halloween costumes are encouraged — bonus points if they’re farm-themed!

events.title: Cedar River Salmon Festival
events.loc: Renton Community Center , 1715 Maple Valley Hwy., Renton
events.desc: Ready to spot some salmon ? They’re migrating up the Cedar River, and this festival invites you to cheer them on and learn more about them. The kids might just be inspired to become salmon scientists!

events.title: Bigfoot Kids’ Book Festival
events.loc: Redmond Senior & Community Center , 8703 160th Ave. N.E., Redmond
events.desc: How many books do your kids ask you to read at night? My daughter requires three, minimum, and we’ve worn out quite a few of her favorites. This literary festival is the perfect opportunity to find a new book to love, with special activities, character and author appearances, and book signings. You can even meet the Gruffalo!

events.title: Outdoor Movie Night & Trunk-or-Treat at McMillin Farm
events.loc: McMillin Farm , 12517 State Route 162 E., Puyallup
events.desc: It’s safe to say my daughter is ready for Halloween. She is counting down with her Halloween advent calendar and has already worn her costume not once, but twice this month. So it’s hard to resist this fun Halloween trunk-or-treat event! There will be festive food and beverages, plus an outdoor showing of the iconic movie “Hocus Pocus.” (Bring blankets and chairs for the movie!)

events.title: Japan Week at Bellevue College
events.loc: Bellevue College , 3000 Landerholm Circle S.E., Bellevue
events.desc: Bellevue College celebrates Japanese culture and history with this full-day celebration. From taiko performances to martial arts demonstrations and themed scavenger hunts, there are plenty of special activities planned. Watch a Japanese musical performance, explore a historical exhibit and shop the market.

events.title: Washington State Parks Free Day
events.desc: Saturday is World Mental Health Day, and Washington state parks are honoring the occasion with free entrance. There are more than 140 state parks, trails and historic sites to explore, no Discover Pass required. Spend the whole day outside!

events.title: TurkFest
events.loc: Seattle Center Armory , 305 Harrison St., Seattle
events.desc: What better way to experience another culture than through its food? I can never resist a piece of baklava and a Turkish coffee, and both will be on offer at this celebration of Turkish culture. There will also be live music and dance performances. And head to the kids corner on the Armory balcony for face painting, games and storytelling.

events.title: Haunted Forest of Maple Valley Family Walk
events.loc: Royal Arch Park , 20821 Renton-Maple Valley Rd. Maple Valley
events.desc: Here’s another opportunity to bring out those Halloween costumes early. Go trick-or-treating along the haunted trails (during the daytime when they are admittedly less scary). You might even get some inspiration for decorating your own yard before trick-or-treaters come.
